original_text: –Stage and Specimen–Thick sections/slices of sample (~1µm) or sample small enough for light to pass through–Samples typically stained with dyes to enhance features–Mounted on glass slide with coverslip–Stage has opening to allow light to pass through
explanation: This slide details requirements for the stage and specimen in light microscopy. Specimens must be prepared as thin sections/slices (~1 micrometer thick) or be small enough to allow light to transmit through them. Samples are typically stained with dyes to enhance structural features, then mounted on a glass slide and secured under a coverslip. The microscope stage features an opening to allow the light to pass through the specimen.

questions.q: Why must specimens for light microscopy be thin (e.g. ~1µm) or small?
opts: To allow light to pass through the sample
To prevent the objective lens from touching them
To absorb the stains and dyes more quickly
questions.exp: The text states: '...sample small enough for light to pass through'.
